sentences.text: 2  ORDER 1.
Learned counsel for the petitioners has filed application to amend the petition.
2. This application is not opposed.
Hence the application is allowed.
Learned counsel for the petitioner to amend the petition forthwith.

3. This petition is filed challenging the proceedings that have been initiated against the petitioners for offenses punishable under sections 498-A, 323, 504 & 506 read with Section 34 of the IPC and Sections 3 & 4 of the D.P. Act.
4. Today, joint application is filed seeking to compound the offences.

The said application reads as follows:
"APPLICATION UNDER SECTION 320 R/W 482 OF THE CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE The Petitioners and the original Complainant / Respondent No.2 in the above case respectfully submits as follows:
1) It is submitted that the Respondent No.2 had filed the Complaint before the Ranebennur Town NC: 2024:KHC-D:949 Police Station and the same was registered in Ranebennur Town P.S. Cr No.127/2023 which is pending before the learned Addl.

Civil Judge (Sr Dn) & C.J.M. Court, Ranebennur, Haveri against the petitioners for the alleged offences punishable U/Sec 498 (A), 323, 504, 506 R/w 34 of IPC & Sec 3,
4 of D P Act.,
2) The Petitioners are Challenging and quashing the C.C. No.2037/2023 (Ranebunner Town P. S. Cr.
No.127/2023) which was registered on 31.08.2023.

It is submitted that with the intervention of Jamat people the matter was settled and the Respondent No.2 is agreed to withdraw the allegations made against the petitioners before the Ranbennur Town Police Station and the Respondent No.2 also agreed to withdraw all allegations against the Petitioners.

It is further submits you that the Petitioner No.1 had paid Rs.8,00,000/-(Eight Lakhs Only) to Respondent No.2 before the Jamat People as a permanent alimony and Respondent No.2 and Petitioner No.1 should file Divorce petition before the competent Court immediately after the Petitioner No.1 should return from Dubai and for the same the Respondent No.2 is ready.
3) It is further submitted that the Petitioner No.1 should not initiate the proceedings against her daughter Ifjz in future & petitioner No.1 should meet & call her daughter once in a month.
5) I further submits you that in future I will not file any civil or criminal cases against the Petitioner No.1 or on their parents and I will not claim any property rights against the petitioner No.1 and their parents in future and also I will not file any maintenance for my daughter Ifja and will not claim any property rights for my daughter against the petitioners.

3

WHEREFORE, the Petitioner and Respondent No.2 in the above case most humbly pray that this Hon'ble Court may be pleased to allow them to Compound the offences and consequently quash the NC: 2024:KHC-D:949 C.C. No. 2037/2023 Ranebunner Town P. S. Cr. No.127/2023) which is pending before the learned Addl Civil Judge (Sr Dn) & C.J.M. Court, Ranebennur, Haveri against the petitioners for the alleged offences punishable U/Sec 498 (A), 323, 504, 506 R/w 34 of IPC &
Sec 3, 4 of D P Act., in the interest of justice and equity."
5.

entities.text: NC: 2024:KHC-D:949 C.C. No. 2037/2023 Ranebunner Town P. S. Cr. No.127/2023)
entities.label: CASE_NUMBER

sentences.text:
In my view, having regard to the fact that this case is essentially a family dispute between the petitioners and the second respondent, there will be no impediment to accept the application and to compound the offences in the light of the judgment in the case of Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Another1.
6.

entities.text: Gian Singh Vs. State of Punjab and Another1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of the above, the petition is allowed and the proceedings in C.C. No.2037/2023 pending before the Addl. Civil Judge (Sr.Dn.) and CJM, Ranebennur, Haveri is quashed.

7. It is however made clear that the rights of the daughter of the second respondent has not been adjudicated upon in these proceedings only the criminal (2012) 10 SCC 303 NC: 2024:KHC-D:949 case registered against the petitioner is allowed to be compounded.
8. The daughter of petitioner No.1 and the second respondent would be at liberty to initiate appropriate proceedings for adjudication of her entitlement, if so permissible in law.
Sd/-
